Federal rower Commission raps 2 Lecember 20, 1975
In addressing the potential for mixing and destratification of LaMe Jocassee, the existence of the second story trout fishery was not known at the time of document draft preparation. (Volume I, Exhibit S "These efforts indicate mixing of noner waters of Lake Josssee will not effect other useful lake purposes such as warm water fishery, " etc.) Later data included in Volume II "rotential Impacts of the Had Greek Pumped - Storage Project on Adjoining Lake and Stream Trout fisheries" does recognize this fishery. The conclusions drawn in this document indicate that the operation of the Lake Jocassee Purped Storage Facility (Units 1 and 2 only) is not disturbing the extent of trout habitat in Lake Jocassee. Fore recent temperature and dissolved oxygen data collected by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service indicates that with the installation of Units 3 and h a significant reduction in suitable summer habitat has occurred. The admitted mixing of at least a portion of Jocassee during operation of Bad Creek now has the potential to disrupt the entire dissolved orygen budget of the lake and, in turn, destroy this important trout fishery. These new aspects of this project must be sufficiently andressed by the applicant. Since no public meetings have been held concerning this project, there new data certainly necessitate such meetings be held to inform the outlic and receive their comments prior to consideration of this license.
Very truly yours,
Robert F. Martin, P. E.
S. C. No. 2928
CC
Duke Power Company
South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources
Discussions of the trout fishery in Lake Jocassee and impacts of the project on cold-water habitat are found in revised Sections 2.2.2.2, 3.2.2.3, and 9.2 of The Bad Creek Final Environmental Impact Statement.
